display.purpose: Level reading inside the glass window; tabular figures.

wordmark.purpose: I-HEAR-YOU, once per surface, top left.

label.purpose: Plate titles, units, and every state word.

data.purpose: dBm, clock, hex and other small measured values.

motion.name: key-travel
motion.purpose: A pressed key moves down 2px; no other transform.

motion.name: lamp-breathe
motion.purpose: Only while a link is coming up.

motion.name: reading-roll
motion.purpose: The level figure slides in the direction of change, like a counter drum; disabled when system animations are off.

components.description: The default machined press key for utility actions.

components.name: Primary Key
components.description: The single action a surface exists for; sealing vermilion with bone text.

components.name: Titled Plate
components.description: The base container: a bordered plate whose label interrupts the top rule.

components.name: Level Window

components.description: Three destinations on a bottom switch plate; the active one carries a vermilion bar.

narrative.overview: The interface is a calibrated domestic instrument: an enamel panel with a glass window, printed scale, a fader per ear, engraved labels, and one vermilion tamper seal. It comes from the utility meter and the audiometer — objects whose whole job is to be read correctly, once, by someone standing in a hallway or sitting in a clinic. The wearer does not admire it; they read it. Two channels, two lives, no cloud. The world is flat and printed: ground, plate, recess; no shadows, no floating cards, no pills. Every control is a machined key with a two-pixel bottom edge, and every value sits in a recessed window behind glass.
keyCharacteristics: Two-channel composition: left and right are two plates on one panel, never a card stack.
Hairline and tonal depth: 1 px rules, recessed windows, no shadows anywhere.
Engraved capitals for labels; counter-drum condensed figures for values.
One accent, used as a seal, an engaged key, or an index mark — never as decoration.
Every write is shown as sent, then as read back.

rules.name: The Seal Rule
rules.body: Sealing vermilion appears on at most three things per screen: the tamper stamp, an engaged control, and the active index. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Two Truths Rule
rules.body: No state is carried by colour or shape alone. A live link is a filled lamp and the word LINKED. Low battery is two cells and the word LOW.

rules.name: The Engraved Capitals Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a thing on the panel is tracked upper case; anything a person says out loud is sentence case at body size.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change on screen is set with tabular figures.

rules.name: The No Floating Rule
rules.body: Nothing hovers. No shadow, no blur, no translucency except the modal scrim.

dos: Do read every state twice: a mark plus a word.
Do keep the panel flat: 1 dp rules and tonal steps carry all separation.
Do set changing numbers in tabular figures and keep the level reading the largest value on screen.
Do show SENT until the aid confirms, then READ BACK.
Do let a CROS read as a transmitter: no program strip, no tap control, no Sound Enhancer.
Do keep light and dark as two hand-set palettes.
donts: Don't use pills, rounded cards above 4 dp, gradients, glass, blur, or drop shadows.
Don't use vermilion as an alarm colour.
Don't use a battery percentage or any invented unit for attenuation.
Don't put cards inside cards, or float a plate on a gradient.
Don't use an icon without a label for anything that changes the aids.
Don't animate a value the aid has not confirmed.
Don't introduce a second accent colour.
